identity.name: INOXGREEN
identity.industry: Renewable Energy O&M & Grid/Evacuation Services (wind + solar asset services)

summary.oneLiner: Inox Green is consolidating into India's largest renewable O&M player via two large inorganic wind-OEM portfolio buys (4.5 GW + 2 GW) on top of organic growth, targeting FY27 EBITDA >INR600 cr (50%-ish margin, near-full cash conversion, INR700 cr tax shield) — but a chunk of current reported profit is acquisition-related "other income" not yet consolidated, so headline quality is soft until the deals formally fold in.

one-line thesis: Inox Green is consolidating into India's largest renewable O&M player via two large inorganic wind-OEM portfolio buys (4.5 GW + 2 GW) on top of organic growth, targeting FY27 EBITDA >INR600 cr (50%-ish margin, near-full cash conversion, INR700 cr tax shield) — but a chunk of current reported profit is acquisition-related "other income" not yet consolidated, so headline quality is soft until the deals formally fold in.
guidance (verify next quarter): FY27 EBITDA upwards of INR600 cr (reaffirmed), driven by full consolidation of the two acquired portfolios + organic adds. Mgmt says ~all of the INR600 cr converts to operating cash profit (no depreciation post-demerger, no finance cost, INR700 cr loss tax-shield).
O&M to rise from ~10% to ~18–20% of group (Inox Wind + Green) revenue mix as acquisitions consolidate.
Watch-item: FY27 EBITDA hinges on accruals from acquired entities effective 1-Apr-26 even if legal merger slips to Q1/Q2 — confirm consolidation actually lands in Q1 FY27 results.
order book & pipeline: O&M portfolio 13+ GWp; pipeline fed by group Inox Clean's 3 GW+/yr additions (14 GW by FY29) and Inox Wind external execution (3.1 GW order book).

Inorganic: two bankrupt wind-OEM O&M portfolios (4.5 GW + ~2 GW) acquired; first NCLT order expected "next couple of weeks," second in 60–90 days. ~50% EBITDA margin on acquired books (OEM substations/evacuation systems).
A "couple of GW" further acquisition targets lined up (≤10–20% of FCF).
segment / subsidiary detail: Core O&M: ~96.5% machine availability; WTG overhaul / life-extension packages launched (high-growth optionality).

Evacuation infra: demerged out into Inox Renewable Solutions (NCLT Ahmedabad approved); IRSL to auto-list post approvals. Removes ~INR1,000 cr gross block and ~INR50–55 cr/yr depreciation from Inox Green.
Digital: exploring "Agent AI" on low value-add roles; Vayuveer/Inox Learning Academy producing ~600 skilled techs/yr (hiring Agniveers).
growth verticals / optionality: Largest renewable O&M co in India near-term; "one of largest globally by 2030."
WTG life-extension/overhaul as a new high-margin service line.
Group "ONE INTEGRATED" flywheel: Inox Clean capacity adds → recurring O&M for Green; Inox Wind equipment supply.
Potential dividend/buyback once two acquisitions consolidate (no policy yet).
margins & cost dynamics: O&M is a ~50% EBITDA-margin business; FY26 ~50% reported, ~45% ex acquisition-related income (per CFO).
Acquisitions add ~50% margin OEM portfolios. Post-demerger depreciation removal materially lifts ROE/ROCE.
Quarterly margin lumpy due to value-add service timing — should be judged annualized.
capex / expansion: Inox Green growth is largely inorganic (portfolio acquisitions) + organic O&M onboarding, capital-light vs manufacturing siblings.
Group capex heavy at Inox Clean (10 GW IPP / 10 GW cell / 10 GW module "10^3" over 15 months) and Inox Wind (power electronics, transformers, cranes in-house) — indirect Green demand driver.
capital allocation: ~INR600 cr invested to acquire the two O&M portfolios (debt-funded; the ~INR40 cr "other income" is the return on that).
Future FCF: first integrate acquisitions, then opportunistic acquisitions (≤10–20% of FCF), with dividend/buyback "in interest of shareholders" to be decided by Board post-consolidation.
risks & watch-items: Earnings quality: large slice of EBITDA/other income is acquisition/debt-related and not-yet-consolidated operating profit — headline ~50% margin drops to ~45% ex that.
Timing risk: FY27 INR600 cr depends on NCLT/EOI approvals landing for both acquired entities (final phases; 60–90 days).

Group execution credibility: investors flagged repeated guidance misses at Inox Wind (MW→revenue guidance switch; INR5,000 cr → INR4,600 cr FY26 on ECS supply-chain/geopolitical delays, PSU payment delays).
Related-party concentration: Inox Clean is the dominant future order source for the group — cycle/governance dependency.
Solar BESS substitution / FDRE battery focus raised as a structural question for wind demand.
management quality / tone: Confident, defensive under pointed minority-shareholder pushback on value destruction and guidance misses; Devansh Jain emphasizes 4-yr value creation, "only Indian wind player that survived with zero haircut," renewable arm "valued north of $10bn." Combative ("don't hold us responsible for a world war"). FY27 75% growth framed as "conservative."
non-obvious takeaways: Sector consolidation thesis: of 5 wind players, "2 allied, 3 bankrupt; we acquired 2 of the 3 bankrupt" — Inox Green is structurally cornering Indian wind O&M.
INR700 cr accumulated-loss tax shield → near-100% cash conversion of FY27 EBITDA.
Evacuation-infra demerger is the real ROE/ROCE lever (gross block + depreciation stripped out), not just operating growth.
Inox Wind's pivot to 75–80% equipment supply (from 100% turnkey 24 months ago) indirectly de-risks Green's parent and working capital.
qoq change log: This quarter (Q4 FY26): O&M op-revenue dipped QoQ (INR78 cr → INR69 cr) on value-add timing; portfolio 13+ GWp; evacuation-infra demerger NCLT-approved (gross block/depreciation removed); two OEM portfolio acquisitions announced (4.5 + 2 GW, ~50% margin); FY27 EBITDA guidance reaffirmed >INR600 cr.

Next-quarter watch items: (1) NCLT order for first acquired entity (~weeks) and EOI close for second (~60–90 days); (2) actual consolidation of acquired EBITDA into Q1 FY27; (3) IRSL listing post-demerger; (4) margin ex acquisition-income trend; (5) any dividend/buyback policy once acquisitions fold in; (6) parent Inox Wind ECS supply-chain/PSU receivable normalization.

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
